## Our issues in Iran today stem from political miscalculation, repeated across decades.
You can trace a straight line from the current war with Iran back to a decision made in 1953, when the[ CIA helped overthrow Mohammad Mosaddegh](https://substack.com/redirect/1c874d09-5fbb-4c3e-9275-d3653f368da8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Iran's democratically elected prime minister, because he had nationalized Iranian oil. Not because he was a tyrant or a threat, but because he wanted his country to keep the oil revenue from its own ground. The operation was called Ajax, it took a few weeks, and when it was over, Mosaddegh, a Harvard-educated lawyer who had appeared on the cover of _Time_ as [Man of the Year](https://substack.com/redirect/3d9b3a71-5874-4127-931f-b5bf3c090228?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), was under house arrest. Washington installed a compliant shah in his place, propped him up for 26 years, and then watched as Iranians overthrew him in a revolution specifically engineered to be everything America didn't want.
The story somehow gets even richer from there.
That same decade, then-President Eisenhower gave Iran civilian nuclear technology as a Cold War goodwill gesture under his "[Atoms for Peace](https://substack.com/redirect/23f99f9a-4498-4667-a2e5-9b9021bc2a3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" program. Eisenhower is regarded as one of our greatest presidents, a five-star general who warned us about the military-industrial complex on his way out the door. And even he handed Iran a nuclear reactor in 1957 because it seemed like a reasonable idea at the time. The stated goal was to share nuclear technology for peaceful purposes. The U.S. supplied a 5-megawatt research reactor that helped establish the Tehran Nuclear Research Center during the Shah's reign.
By the 1970s, the U.S. was actively helping the shah [develop full nuclear energy capability](https://substack.com/redirect/b6b00773-523c-4bfb-ad04-fc26c928ca73?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- because he was our guy, and our guy should have whatever he needed. Then the Iranian Revolution happened, the shah fled, and the program we'd spent two decades enthusiastically building became the single greatest national security threat in the Middle East we'd spend the next 47 years trying to dismantle.
The same nuclear program that the Obama administration spent years negotiating to contain -- and got absolutely savaged politically for doing so -- exists in part because of decisions made in Washington in 1957. The JCPOA, the deal negotiated and signed by the five UN Security Council members plus Germany, ended the Iranian nuclear enrichment program and established IAEA inspections (["trust, but verify"](https://substack.com/redirect/55420854-60b4-4070-8139-40ef3f0fa7ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for you Reagan fans) in exchange for lifting sanctions, and it was working until our sitting President called the ["worst deal"](https://substack.com/redirect/8b361b1a-4b73-450c-a05e-66265e7bf6e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in American diplomatic history. He unilaterally ripped it up and reimposed sanctions once again. This deal was an attempt to clean up a mess that started when Washington handed Iran a reactor in 1957. Somehow, that seems to get lost in the context of the current situation.
So, yeah. This might come as a major surprise to many of you reading this.

We too often create our own problems, then spend half a century trying to fix them while criticizing the people attempting to manage them diplomatically. If that doesn't work, too many bureaucrats who've never worn the cloth of this country are quick to send our sons and daughters back to war to clean up Washington DC's mess, which is where we are now.
None of this is on our servicemembers serving overseas. Not one bit of it.
We're good at mythologizing our troops when the stakes are low. The parades, the "thank you for your service," the halftime tributes. We're worse at the actual accounting of what we asked these people to do, under what circumstances, in whose interest, and what we owe them when it's over.
The men and women serving right now didn't vote on any of this -- in fact, military personnel are prohibited from engaging in partisan political activity under Defense Department regulations. They simply chose to put on a uniform and went where they were told because that's what they signed up to do, and because the oath they took doesn't come with an asterisk that says "unless the politics get complicated."
Whatever one thinks of this war, our troops deserve to be respected as human beings who made a commitment to something larger than themselves.
Service members take an oath to the Constitution before the mission is defined. They depend on our political leadership in Washington to do right by them and our military history as a nation is one of a reluctant warrior. They commit without knowing the theater, the terms of engagement, the intelligence quality, or the exit strategy. The country benefits from that certainty and then frequently fails to honor it -- sometimes with outright hostility, as it did after Vietnam, and sometimes with what Iraq produced instead: a kind of hollow "support the troops" shorthand that fills bumper stickers but doesn't translate into jobs, mental health resources, or genuine inclusion in civilian private-sector leadership.
One of my favorite books (and writers) is Sebastian Junger's _[Tribe: On Homecoming and Belonging](https://substack.com/redirect/cec37625-f9f1-44eb-b658-5222cbf139ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ,_ where he argues that returning veterans struggle not just with trauma, but with the alienation of our modern, individualistic society preoccupied with the attention economy -- which stands in stark contrast to the tight-knit, purposeful "tribe" of the U.S. military. Junger believes that celebrating troops upon their return -- which was historically the norm -- fosters a more unified society and creates community-based support systems, rather than bureaucratic care outsourced to the VA. Too often we take a "whole of government" approach to our returning veterans rather than a "whole of nation" one.
Less than [1%](https://substack.com/redirect/6ecaa445-2b44-46b9-a01e-b6852969eeaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Americans currently serve. Most still [view the military favorably](https://substack.com/redirect/1fac72b3-06c3-41c5-9f92-9d3f1e1b6171?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- 60%, according to Pew Research -- but that number drops to 43% among adults under 30, the only age group where more people hold a negative view than a positive one.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4c19c8d3-7e2a-46c7-b090-9cea6053f925?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So the next time you find yourself angry about this war, aim that anger in the right direction. Toward the decision-makers, the architects, the people who built the problem and handed it to the current generation of warriors to solve. Not toward the twenty-something patriot somewhere over the Strait of Hormuz who is doing, with remarkable courage, exactly what his or her country asked them to do on behalf of our nation.

Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Folks: The United States Postal Service is being pushed toward a financial breaking point that could cause it to run out of cash as soon as February of next year, and only Congress can fix it.
The Postmaster General has warned that the current financial crisis at USPS could “ lead to the end of the Postal Service as we know it” if lawmakers fail to act. This crisis did not come out of nowhere. It is the result of years of bad postal policy decisions that drained billions from the Postal Service and tied its hands.
Donald Trump and his greedy corporate buddies would love to see a privatized Postal Service. They want to throw entire communities under the bus, outsource delivery, and sell the post office off piecemeal to make millions. We cannot allow that to happen. It would mean higher costs for families, the risk of service shutdowns for rural communities, and the loss of a public institution that guarantees universal access to mail.
Send your letter now: Congress must remove the financial barriers that will allow USPS to stabilize its finances and create a sustainable future >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-the-privatization-of-the-usps/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
START WRITING NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-the-privatization-of-the-usps/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
In 2022, the Postal Service Reform Act was one step that ended requirements such as the pre-funding of retiree health benefits and restrictions on pricing and some service expansion.
It is time to completely untie the Postal Service’s hands and allow the agency to fully manage benefit and retirement funds, pension investments, and to extend the agency’s borrowing authority that hasn’t been adjusted for inflation since 1992. Congress must reverse the law restricting the USPS from providing new services that could generate new streams of revenue.
The Postal Service is not supposed to be a profit machine. It is a lifeline for communities across the country. Removing these policy restrictions will allow the Postal Service to continue delivering our mail and serving the public effectively, saving the agency billions of dollars per year.
Take action to save the Post Office! Demand Congress reverse bad postal policy and stop privatization now >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-the-privatization-of-the-usps/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]

_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=2067%2E259176%2E6hSapf) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=2067%2E259176%2E6hSapf)_

I want you to know that I never take your support and confidence for granted. And while the attacks on our work to uphold the values we share keep mounting — and will only continue to do so — your continued support motivates me to never back down from this fight. **For the sake of our democracy. I've never been afraid of a fight, friend.
I've been arrested on the steps of the Capitol. I've been called a traitor. I've been written off, dismissed, and underestimated more times than I can count. And every single time, I got back up because I knew that what we were fighting for was bigger than any one of us.
Every movement that has ever changed the world — from civil rights to women’s liberation to climate justice — started because people refused to stay quiet.
_That rebellious spirit is what’s needed right now._
Because let’s be real: The news under the Trump administration is a never-ending barrage of chaos. Attack after attack on our core democratic institutions. Climate protections ripped away. Fundamental freedoms undermined.
**But after decades of fighting, I’ve learned that the feeling of being small is exactly what they want.**
They want us to believe we’re powerless and hopeless. Joke’s on them because we refuse to give them that satisfaction.
We don’t need to be the biggest, the loudest, or the wealthiest. We just need to keep showing up. That’s why I started the Jane Fonda Climate PAC. To take the spirit of rebellion into the halls of power — by resisting the fossil fuel industry’s influence and electing climate champions who will fight for people, not corporate profits.
**But this work takes resources. And that’s why I am asking for your help.[If you believe, like I do, that resistance is more necessary than ever, I’m humbly asking you to please contribute whatever you can before our fundraising deadline this Wednesday. clean_body: We won’t give them the satisfaction. | | = = | = I've never been afraid of a fight, friend. I've been arrested on the steps of the Capitol. I've been called a traitor. I've been written off, dismissed, and underestimated more times than I can count. And every single time, I got back up because I knew that what we were fighting for was bigger than any one of us. Every movement that has ever changed the world — from civil rights to women’s liberation to climate justice — started because people refused to stay quiet. That rebellious spirit is what’s needed right now. Because let’s be real: The news under the Trump administration is a never-ending barrage of chaos. Attack after attack on our core democratic institutions. Climate protections ripped away. Fundamental freedoms undermined. But after decades of fighting, I’ve learned that the feeling of being small is exactly what they want. They want us to believe we’re powerless and hopeless. Joke’s on them because we refuse to give them that satisfaction. We don’t need to be the biggest, the loudest, or the wealthiest. We just need to keep showing up. That’s why I started the Jane Fonda Climate PAC. To take the spirit of rebellion into the halls of power — by resisting the fossil fuel industry’s influence and electing climate champions who will fight for people, not corporate profits. But this work takes resources. I want to take a moment and share with you the **pathway of VICTORY** for #[LahmeyerForCongress](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=28779607.14539.1.9c1698baa29d280abdaa9aec856d5600). In 2018, there was a very crowded field of Republican candidates running for CD1. **Kevin Hern** got into the runoff with **22.7% of the vote** and then went on to win the runoff and general election. His path to victory is also our path to victory. The race I am in is a very crowded field (12 candidates!) but this crowded field helps us. When I ran for Senate in 2022, we **over performed** beyond everyone's expectations. All the polls and experts said we would be lucky to break 10%. Across the state of Oklahoma we actually got 26% of the vote but that's not as exciting as what I am about to share with you. In 2022, I received around **32% of the vote in Congressional District 1**. That means, if I can hold the base of voters that already voted for me once then we could find ourselves in the runoff which positions us for victory like **Congressman Kevin Hern** in 2018. Here are the advantages that #[LahmeyerForCongress](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=28779607.14540.1.f0982b920a0cd802effadca0b29bf31d) has against all the other candidates that are running. **First** , my name has appeared already on a ballot across CD1 (name ID is a major factor in primary elections). **Second** , there are only 64 days until the election on June 16 which helps us tremendously because it will be very difficult for all the candidates to introduce themselves to the voters across the entire district. **Third** , I have already received enough votes in this district to position me for the runoff if we can hold our base. I truly believe that we are positioned to win this election. In order to do so, we need to make sure our base of voters know that I am in it and what I will do if I was fortunate enough to be elected. I am running for Congress in Oklahoma's 1st District to do several things: **-Keep Our Borders Secure** **-Remove Illegal Criminals From Our Streets** **-Help Make Living In America Affordable For Americans** **-Not Allowing The Chinese Communist Party To Own American Farmland** **-Ensuring That Sharia Law Never Takes Root In Our Nation** Please consider making a donation to our efforts to help us to run more ads on TV, radio and print. I want to thank the over **600 individual donors** who partnered with us so far. You can help us win this election by donating at [www.jacksonlahmeyer.com](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=28779607.14541.1.2179a3e62965bc5d4fa462578beee39f) Your help allows us to be on TV, radio and send out mailers. Also, please consider posting on social media that you support #[LahmeyerForCongress](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=28779607.14542.1.4484d55f0ee189d8a316c2b2a811d4cc) this makes a BIG difference. I promise that if you will help me get elected that I will do my very best to make you proud. Thank you,
Jackson Lahmeyer

| | |

| | | | [|

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** April 13, 2026
**Will the Real Bill Cassidy Please Stand Up?**_Bombshell Report Exposes Cassidy's Two-Faced Campaign_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** – Bill Cassidy has a problem. He has burned through millions of dollars on television telling Louisiana Republicans he is a conservative they can trust. But according to a [bombshell new report](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=cd2cf55c89&e=95355a072c), he is telling Democrats the exact opposite in private conversations.
Last week, progressive columnist Robert Mann reported that Cassidy and his allies have been urging Democrats to switch parties, register as Republicans, and vote for Cassidy in the May 16 primary, and that Cassidy personally called Mann to make the case himself.
Cassidy has previously tried to frame that outreach as a routine response to Louisiana's new closed primary system. Mann's reporting blows that cover story apart.
According to Mann, the argument Cassidy is privately making to Democrats is: "I'm really not as crazy and MAGA-like as I've had to sound over the past year and a half."
And implicit in his pitch, as Mann described it, is this: "To win back enough MAGA voters to capture the nomination, I need to persuade voters that Letlow is the real liberal. But I hope you'll understand that I'm the real moderate."
Three days later, and Cassidy still has not addressed the report.
If the report is false, Cassidy should say so clearly and immediately.
If it is true, Republican voters deserve to know why their senator is spending millions selling them a version of himself he privately describes as an act, and why he is asking the Democrats to rescue him from his own party's primary.
**THE CHOICE IS CLEAR** Julia Letlow is the Trump-endorsed conservative in this race. Bill Cassidy is the senator who voted to convict President Trump and, according to Mann's reporting, has been privately telling Democrats that his conservative campaign is an act, that his attacks on Julia Letlow are a political tactic, and that he needs the other party to rescue him from his own party's voters.
He needs to answer one simple question: which Bill Cassidy is the real one?
On May 16, Louisiana Republicans will answer for him.

name: VoteVets.org
subject: How Trump Lost the Iran War
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS, VOTEVETS
body:
What we are seeing is not strategy, it is improvisation.
#
After a weekend of failed negotiations in Pakistan, we think you'll get a lot from reading Major General (Ret.) Paul Eaton's most recent piece in Substack.
[**How Trump Lost the Iran War**](https://act.votevets.org/go/19803?source=em260413-1-120&refcode2=35081.3013755.sXzlbr&t=1&akid=35081%2E3013755%2EsXzlbr)
I have spent a career planning military operations and evaluating the operations of others. The first question any competent military planner asks before committing forces is not “can we hit the target?” The United States military can always hit the target. The question is: to what end? What is the strategic objective? What happens on Day 4, 5, 6 and so on? What does success look like? How do we know when we’ve achieved it? And how do we get out?
In forty days of a war of choice (not necessity) with Iran, the Trump administration never answered any of those questions. Not once.
What we got instead was a pattern that repeated itself from the first week to the last: a threat, followed by bombing, followed by a frantic search for an offramp that didn’t exist because no one had built one.
What we are seeing is not strategy, it is improvisation. It is what we are seeing today with the naval blockade. And when you improvise a war, people die and families are left to wonder why.
Thank you for reading,
The team at VoteVets

body:
I recently came across a striking statistic... 72% of J6 defendants were military veterans or first responders.
---
[View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e926879/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvRXFjZ05aRVlucQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA0MTM/LbmNsRFpRU3Jlbg/qP2hpZHM9bmNuekJTS0JvaXhieWVscw/gad0Yag/s1tb16210ae)

[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

Patriot,

I recently came across a striking statistic.

**72% of J6 defendants were military veterans or first responders.**

And while courts often consider prior service as a factor for lighter sentences, the prosecutors and judges in these cases used their veteran or first responder status to argue for _**harsher penalties**_.

_Is this how our criminal justice system thanks them for their service?_

I’ve always honored those who serve. We are living the American dream _because_ of them. The way these patriots were treated is a grave injustice.

And while President Trump has pardoned almost all of the J6 defendants, they still haven’t received justice.

The lives and reputations of these patriots remain shattered from the lost years to the consistent government and mainstream media smear campaign they endured.

That’s why I’m proud to support Stand in the Gap.

This remarkable organization provides real, practical help, like rent money, job training, transportation, legal referrals, trauma counseling, and health insurance, to help these persecuted patriots move on with their lives.

[If you believe in liberty, in due process, and in standing up for our fellow Americans, I hope you’ll make a donation to Stand in the Gap today. >>](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
[Donate](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
Before January 6th, many of these patriots were unaware of just how broken the American justice system truly was.
Even after being pardoned, many J6 defendants still face...
* Difficulties finding a job
* Loss of rights, like the right to vote or the right to own a firearm
* Harassment on social media and in their personal lives
* Strained family relationships due to lost time in prison
* And even homelessness.

For many, returning to some semblance of a normal life is overwhelming.

**Stand in the Gap is committed to being a comprehensive support system for J6 defendants and their families by providing essential resources to help these American patriots heal physically, mentally, emotionally, and spiritually.**

Stand in the Gap believes in second chances, providing support to individuals transitioning back into society after incarceration, and working towards a more forward-thinking and restorative prison system that sends non-violent offenders into the world better off than they were when they went in.

Through their programs, partnerships, and advocacy efforts, they are making a lasting impact on the lives of those in need.

**There are nearly 1,600 Americans who are looking for a second chance.**

Let’s show these patriots they’re not forgotten.

[Will you help J6 defendants get back on their feet by donating $10, $35, $50, or even $100 to Stand in the Gap today? >>](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
[Donate $10](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $35](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $50](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $100](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $250](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $500](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $1,000](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate Any Amount](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
This isn’t about politics. It’s about justice.

These are real Americans — veterans, first responders, fathers, mothers, hard-working citizens — who exercised their First Amendment rights and were persecuted for their political beliefs.

_**If we don’t fight for our fellow patriots now, who will?**_

When you donate to Stand in the Gap, you’re not just defending individuals. _You are defending the soul of our country_.

**As long as there’s breath in my lungs and truth in my heart, I’ll be singing to honor veterans and first responders. I hope you’ll join me by taking action right now.**
[Donate](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
For faith, freedom, and country,

John Rich

motivate young voters, first-time voters, and voters of color to show

Peter. And if the people reading

all this momentum, will you chip in your first donation today to help us
build the surge we need? Even $1 helps. Seriously.

| | Friend,
---
| | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus.

He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness.

And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible.

I saw it up close -- _Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. _

But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything.

_**He started observing the Sabbath. **_

Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance.

_But as an act of obedience. _

As a way of saying, **_" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." _**

Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped.

He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield.

No email. No media. No work.

He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children.

It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much.

But over time, it changed him.

And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned...

This was Charlie's final message. His final act of trust.

name: Sara Jacobs
subject: Can you make an 8-hour drive to vote?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Sara Jacobs for Congress
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]
Donald Trump's SAVE Act would make it significantly harder for Americans to vote — not non-citizens, not fraudsters, but real, everyday Americans.
Think about the married woman who changed her name and doesn’t have a certified copy of her marriage license on hand. Under this bill, her voter registration could be at risk. Eight in 10 women in this country who marry change their last name, meaning more than 60 million women could be impacted.
Think about the rural voter who lives hours from the nearest registration office. In some parts of this country, re-registering under this bill could mean an 8-hour round trip.
Think about the hourly worker who can't get time off to sort out their documents, re-register, or vote in-person.
This bill isn't about election security — voter fraud is already incredibly rare. And it is already illegal for non-citizens to vote in federal elections, with strict penalties, including deportation.
This bill is about making it harder to vote right before the midterms — hitting rural voters, women, hourly workers, younger voters, and people of color the hardest.
So here's what I'm asking you to do:
1. Talk to someone outside your bubble. A family member in a rural area. A friend in a red state. Someone who might not be seeing accurate information about what this bill actually means for them. Share what you know, because these conversations matter a lot.
2. Call the Senate. The Capitol switchboard is (202) 224-3121. Tell any senator you can reach — especially Republican senators — that you strongly oppose the SAVE Act, and urge them to vote NO.
We have stopped this bill before because of public pressure. We can do it again — but only if enough people speak up, and speak up loudly.
Thank you for being one of them.
–Sara

I refuse to shy away from tough conversations on the campaign trail.
From the moment we launched this campaign, we knew we couldn’t do it alone. This is one of the most competitive districts in the country—and the billionaires and corporations who control our politics are going to do everything they can to buy this seat. To fight back, we need to build a campaign that brings together people from all walks of life.
That means that when I’m out talking to folks in coffee shops, union halls, or on someone’s front porch, I will take the time to have a hard conversation.
I know that my neighbors and I have so much more in common than what divides us—no matter their political party, religion, age, race, or any other factor.
If we can have honest, good-faith conversations, then most of us can find something we can agree on. Right now, many of us can agree that costs need to come down. We can agree that our healthcare system and immigration system are broken. We can agree that our children should all have the chance to succeed.
No one is written off in my book. Everyone counts.
We have four months to prove this district can't be bought. Every conversation we have between now and then gets us closer to winning and bringing better leadership to Washington, D.C., but we need the resources to keep having the conversations in the first place. body:
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_YkfwvxMpXgwIVT6d1UY74sxuR1rMyZbDmCp3thhUkNYDrsR13gpy42695ja85ESb2S1MMgElmD5Ac15UL1AUP67CCaBNyhFAPnk9VYyQy6uaZqGt13Ds2MS4zPPrl3OxJOgh_ZgvSbOs669DlMpholQvZ2vsx96i7-gyTXVZH_oAHaKh2d1JrjZdFI6BI3HSt0OI2mKeY07xenmGCgBVkE4n6oNhla-&c=zhGB8PK8HjnIcrt419v5dD68VUIv5zc_0ve9-Y6sDnRTQR2Re0mn0Q==&ch=_oxlTgqVCGDJk7fbTWA2dtkBZ4__G1pYCBjRca2KeY2Zguh7tM8srg==)

Peter,
We did something different in Wisconsin, and people are sitting up and taking notice.
With a smaller budget than our Pennsylvania Supreme Court race in 2025, we couldn't run a full field and TV campaign. Traditional organizers. Mailers. Ads on every screen.
That wasn't in the cards.
So instead of doing less of what everyone else does, we did something no one else was doing.
Our co-founder Joe Bachman was just interviewed by Wisconsin Public Radio about the cutting-edge voter contact technology we deployed in the state and how it helped us punch way above our weight:

---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_YkfwvxMpXgwIVT6d1UY74sxuR1rMyZbDmCp3thhUkNYDrsR13gpy42695ja85ESb2S1MMgElmD5Ac15UL1AUP67CCaBNyhFAPnk9VYyQy6uaZqGt13Ds2MS4zPPrl3OxJOgh_ZgvSbOs669DlMpholQvZ2vsx96i7-gyTXVZH_oAHaKh2d1JrjZdFI6BI3HSt0OI2mKeY07xenmGCgBVlIzNacqzFkD&c=zhGB8PK8HjnIcrt419v5dD68VUIv5zc_0ve9-Y6sDnRTQR2Re0mn0Q==&ch=_oxlTgqVCGDJk7fbTWA2dtkBZ4__G1pYCBjRca2KeY2Zguh7tM8srg==)
---

Here's the core idea: every Democrat deserves an organizer in their pocket.
An actual, interactive tool built specifically to talk a voter through exactly what they needed to know. Where to vote, what ID to bring, how the process works. One that could speak to Chris Taylor's record and positions on the issues. One that could answer questions with accurate information, at any hour, at a massive scale: we used it to reach over 1 million voters.
We share the concerns about AI's energy demands, economic disruption, and impact on workers. That's why we worked with our partners at Convos to keep our footprint minimal. And for what it's worth: this approach has a smaller environmental impact than a large mailer campaign.
AI is becoming a bigger part of political campaigns. As we read stories about deepfakes and misinformation, Defend Our Courts is proud to lead the way in using this technology responsibly and transparently to have real conversations with the voters we need to reach.
This also isn't about replacing the field organizers and volunteers who are the backbone of our democracy. It's about giving them a force multiplier. Reaching voters they couldn't reach. Having conversations that would otherwise never happen.
Wisconsin showed it can work and we couldn't have done it without you.
Tens of thousands of Democrats across the country pitched in to fuel this work. You made a difference in a race that far too few people were paying attention to.
Court races are like that. Under the radar. Underestimated. Until suddenly they're not.
2026 will have more high-stakes judicial races, with the same type of stakes as Wisconsin and Pennsylvania. We want to continue bringing our winning formula to key races on a national scale. But we need your continued support to do it:
[If you believe in what we're building and what we proved is possible, can we count on you to chip in $25, $15, or whatever you can spare today to help us build for more court battles in 2026?](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_YkfwvxMpXgwIVT6d1UY74sxuR1rMyZbDmCp3thhUkNYDrsR13gpy42695ja85ESXzx4dn1HNBQnes-C2zyJ6IYpijdr020CsEX5I8Dj2dvzDHPge8_frJ9YegcDH6sZWWy731BD08cOIq4tjZfnSB-gpXVP-BqXvqiKqOkuj3zDFtHTtJ5jGdQOr-JjJkWn-XAAvoW14J7Bfbm5BfVQ9a0O4PUXPtS48Hpj9RaPYOhJ6PSLeha7nQ==&c=zhGB8PK8HjnIcrt419v5dD68VUIv5zc_0ve9-Y6sDnRTQR2Re0mn0Q==&ch=_oxlTgqVCGDJk7fbTWA2dtkBZ4__G1pYCBjRca2KeY2Zguh7tM8srg==)

> When that fateful call went out that one of America's F-15 fighter jets had taken enemy fire, and both aviators on board were forced to eject over enemy territory, deep behind enemy lines in Iran, almost immediately, the legendary Air Force Combat Search and Rescue team (CSAR) and Joint Special Operations Command (JSOC) sprang into action. Within a matter of seconds, the Air Force's elite rescue team started the process of doing what it does best, sniffing out downed pilots like hungry bloodhounds that haven't eaten for days.
> [Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.CCXoyUubCtviFoAt1EmI0EeplLWZddaN4R6Ofr1kwMQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=194089699)
>
> In coordination with ground intelligence provided by the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), this highly dedicated and incredibly motivated team of sophisticated warriors serving our nation, live and breathe for this precise moment in time and immediately began its task. The opportunity to maneuver through hellish landscapes while dodging enemy fire, simply for the opportunity to retrieve downed pilots or servicemembers that might otherwise be captured or killed; this is how these brave warriors choose to earn their paychecks.
>
> Their preparation and training are an understated masterclass in strategic planning, tenacity, and sheer fortitude and unwavering courage; and nobody does it better than them. Their motto, "These Things We Do, That Others May Live" should tell you everything you need to know about them. From the moment they received the call out, to the moment their rotor blades begin cutting through the air, their message was abundantly clear; we're coming for you, and we're not leaving without you.
> | [](https://substack.com/redirect/ba8c8960-88ca-4788-9b1e-df719fd5bf46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
> ---|---|---
> CSAR personnel undergo incredibly rigorous training, lasting nearly two years. This includes parachuting proficiency, advanced diving techniques, innovative survival methods, resistance and escape methods, advanced tracking systems, and full paramedic certification. Their motto underscores the risks and sacrifices these elite teams undertake to rescue downed pilots, isolated troops, or other assets in combat zones, operating in the most hostile environments in ghostly fashion.
>
> These aren't your run of the mill search teams with flashlights and first aid kits; they are the elite of the elite within America's Armed Forces. Its primary mission is to study special operations requirements, develop tactics, and conduct high priority missions globally on a moment's notice. Their worldwide stations are highly classified, and these ethereal specialists can be anywhere within the world within a matter of hours.
>
> From the moment CIA ground intel pinpointed the downed Airmen's approximate locations every precious second mattered. Rescue plans were devised for each downed aviator; insertion points were mapped out to the millimeter, cover points were created from every angle imaginable, and American air support was synchronized to provide both high and low flying umbrella like protection. What made these missions especially dire was that the aviators were miles apart, each suffering from a variety of injuries sustained during ejection, and subsequent landing as the barbaric IRGC closed in on their locations.
>
> But let's get one thing straight about this elite team of rescuers; they are straight out of central casting. As their helicopters lifted off, every crew member knew the stakes. They weren't just tracking their downed pilots; they were showing the world American resilience and that unbreakable bond that's says we never leave a man behind.
>
> The CSAR team doesn't just rescue pilots, they embody the doctrine that no mission is too difficult and no environment too hostile. Courage is simply their baseline; a unique skillset that's engineered for success in scenarios where the odds are stacked against them. They laugh in the face of danger because they know they've trained harder, pushed further, and are willing to bleed out for every inch of airspace and every life they recover from enemy hands.
> | [](https://substack.com/redirect/1058f940-79b2-46b0-94a9-a73ee284225f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
> ---|---|---
> During this mission, most of the world held their collective breath and thought these downed pilots were as good as gone, to be used as propaganda tools by the IRGC, and tortured in ways we simply cannot imagine. But as the CSAR crew lifted off in recovery mode, every one of them knew the stakes. Once on the ground and in theatre, the team moved swiftly through the terrain like a pack of wolves on the scent of their prey, with precision, unapologetic hostility and zero room for error.
>
> After a few perilous days, both downed aviators were safely recovered and touched back down on friendly soil. At this point, the entire CSAR team exhaled a breath they'd been holding in for about 72 hours; a mixture of relief, pride, and a well-deserved smug satisfaction that comes with pulling off the impossible under the worst of circumstances. For three days their brethren were hunted and faced certain death if captured, but due to the unbreakable bond that says, "we never leave a man behind," the two rescued aviators will see their families once again, thanks to the heroics of those fearless CSAR operators who vow to always have their six.

* * *
By now, I'm sure you've seen that Donald Trump took it upon himself to not only attack Pope Leo by name, but also post an insane AI-generated image of himself as Jesus Christ healing the sick. It's offensive, it's bizarre, and it says a lot more about him than I think he realizes.
But there's a deeper conversation here--not just about Trump, but about what he represents, how his movement operates, and why Catholicism, at this moment, poses a real threat to the version of Christianity that many in MAGA are trying to promote.
For those who don't know, I'm a practicing Catholic with a complicated relationship with my faith. I found my way back to it when Pope Francis ascended, and I started going back to church more consistently after Pope Leo took over the Vatican last year. My faith matters to me. It shapes how I see the world, how I try to show up for my family, and why I believe in the kind of politics I do.
I can trace most of my values back to that foundation--even during the periods when I drifted from it.
And that's what makes this moment feel so stark.
Because when you compare that to Donald Trump, there's no real evidence of any grounding in faith beyond himself. There's no consistency, no humility, no sense of moral framework that extends beyond loyalty and power. That's not a partisan critique--it's an observation about how he moves through the world.
And yet, for years now, people who claim to be motivated politically by Christianity have aligned themselves with him because he delivered results. They saw an opportunity to advance their agenda, and they took it. On their own terms, it's been effective--policy wins, overturning Roe v. Wade, political power and influence in the government.
But that alliance has always been transactional. And now it's starting to show its limits.
Because Trump doesn't recognize any authority higher than himself. Not institutions, not traditions, and certainly not religious leadership that challenges him.
That's where Pope Leo comes in--and why this moment matters.
For the first time, we have an American pope. Someone who speaks in our cultural language, who understands this country not as an outsider looking in, but as someone who comes from it. I still remember crying when I learned we were going to have an American pope from Chicago. That meant something to me in a way I didn't expect.
And now, that same pope--and other Catholic leaders--are speaking clearly about issues like war, economic inequality, and immigration. Not as politicians, but as moral voices. As people calling for restraint, dignity, and care for others.
That creates a direct contrast.
Not just between two individuals, but between two visions of what faith in public life looks like.
One is rooted in power--using religion as a tool to justify dominance, exclusion, and control.

* * *
The other treats faith as a constraint--something that calls for humility, service, and moral accountability, even when it's inconvenient.
That version isn't perfect. But it asks something fundamentally different, especially of power.
That contrast is uncomfortable for people who have spent years blurring the line between faith and political identity.
Because if faith becomes something that can challenge power instead of reinforce it, then it stops being as useful to those who've built their influence around it.
That's why you're seeing such a mixed reaction from MAGA right now.
Some are suddenly outraged. Others are defending Trump. Some are trying to ignore it altogether and hope it goes away.
But underneath all of that is the same tension: what happens when faith stops serving the people in power and starts questioning it?
Because Trump doesn't recognize any authority higher than himself. Not institutions, not traditions, and certainly not religious leadership that challenges him.
But this time, the target isn't just a political opponent or an influencer he's mad at. It's a religious leader with global credibility, speaking to hundreds of millions of people who take their faith seriously.
That's different.
And it's why this moment feels bigger than a stupid, yet blasphemous, AI meme.
It's exposing the limits of an alliance that was always built on convenience rather than shared conviction.
And in doing so, it creates an opening.
Because for too long, Democrats have been hesitant to talk about faith in public life, ceding that ground entirely to the right. And in doing so, we've allowed a narrow, often distorted version of Christianity to define what faith in politics looks like.
It doesn't have to be that way.
You don't have to be religious to see the value in moral language that emphasizes dignity, care, and responsibility. And if you are religious, you shouldn't feel like you have to check that part of yourself at the door to participate in politics.
We can't let faith be something that's owned, weaponized, and narrowed by one movement.
It's bigger than that.
And moments like this--when the contradictions are so visible--give us a chance to say so.
Not by shouting louder, but by being clearer about what we believe and why.
Because at the end of the day, this isn't just about Donald Trump or Pope Leo.
It's about which version of faith we're willing to accept in public life--one that bends to power, or one that challenges it.
That's the choice in front of us.
And that choice is becoming harder to ignore.

clean_body: The clash between power-driven politics and a competing moral authority. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? What happens when faith starts questioning power? | | | Apr 13 | | | | | | | | | | | | By now, I'm sure you've seen that Donald Trump took it upon himself to not only attack Pope Leo by name, but also post an insane AI-generated image of himself as Jesus Christ healing the sick. It's offensive, it's bizarre, and it says a lot more about him than I think he realizes. But there's a deeper conversation here--not just about Trump, but about what he represents, how his movement operates, and why Catholicism, at this moment, poses a real threat to the version of Christianity that many in MAGA are trying to promote. For those who don't know, I'm a practicing Catholic with a complicated relationship with my faith. I found my way back to it when Pope Francis ascended, and I started going back to church more consistently after Pope Leo took over the Vatican last year. My faith matters to me. It shapes how I see the world, how I try to show up for my family, and why I believe in the kind of politics I do. I can trace most of my values back to that foundation--even during the periods when I drifted from it. And that's what makes this moment feel so stark. Because when you compare that to Donald Trump, there's no real evidence of any grounding in faith beyond himself. There's no consistency, no humility, no sense of moral framework that extends beyond loyalty and power. That's not a partisan critique--it's an observation about how he moves through the world. And yet, for years now, people who claim to be motivated politically by Christianity have aligned themselves with him because he delivered results. They saw an opportunity to advance their agenda, and they took it. On their own terms, it's been effective--policy wins, overturning Roe v. Wade, political power and influence in the government. But that alliance has always been transactional. And now it's starting to show its limits. Because Trump doesn't recognize any authority higher than himself. Not institutions, not traditions, and certainly not religious leadership that challenges him. That's where Pope Leo comes in--and why this moment matters. For the first time, we have an American pope. Someone who speaks in our cultural language, who understands this country not as an outsider looking in, but as someone who comes from it. I still remember crying when I learned we were going to have an American pope from Chicago. That meant something to me in a way I didn't expect. And now, that same pope--and other Catholic leaders--are speaking clearly about issues like war, economic inequality, and immigration. Not as politicians, but as moral voices. As people calling for restraint, dignity, and care for others. That creates a direct contrast. Not just between two individuals, but between two visions of what faith in public life looks like. One is rooted in power--using religion as a tool to justify dominance, exclusion, and control. * The other treats faith as a constraint--something that calls for humility, service, and moral accountability, even when it's inconvenient. That version isn't perfect. But it asks something fundamentally different, especially of power. That contrast is uncomfortable for people who have spent years blurring the line between faith and political identity. Because if faith becomes something that can challenge power instead of reinforce it, then it stops being as useful to those who've built their influence around it. That's why you're seeing such a mixed reaction from MAGA right now. Some are suddenly outraged. Others are defending Trump. Some are trying to ignore it altogether and hope it goes away. But underneath all of that is the same tension: what happens when faith stops serving the people in power and starts questioning it? Because Trump doesn't recognize any authority higher than himself. Not institutions, not traditions, and certainly not religious leadership that challenges him. But this time, the target isn't just a political opponent or an influencer he's mad at. It's a religious leader with global credibility, speaking to hundreds of millions of people who take their faith seriously. That's different. And it's why this moment feels bigger than a stupid, yet blasphemous, AI meme. It's exposing the limits of an alliance that was always built on convenience rather than shared conviction. And in doing so, it creates an opening. Because for too long, Democrats have been hesitant to talk about faith in public life, ceding that ground entirely to the right. And in doing so, we've allowed a narrow, often distorted version of Christianity to define what faith in politics looks like. It doesn't have to be that way. You don't have to be religious to see the value in moral language that emphasizes dignity, care, and responsibility. And if you are religious, you shouldn't feel like you have to check that part of yourself at the door to participate in politics. We can't let faith be something that's owned, weaponized, and narrowed by one movement. It's bigger than that. And moments like this--when the contradictions are so visible--give us a chance to say so. Not by shouting louder, but by being clearer about what we believe and why. Because at the end of the day, this isn't just about Donald Trump or Pope Leo. It's about which version of faith we're willing to accept in public life--one that bends to power, or one that challenges it. That's the choice in front of us. And that choice is becoming harder to ignore. Mike Nellis is a Democratic strategist and entrepreneur who has raised over $1 billion for Democratic campaigns and causes. Hi there,
**I’m Wellesley, the campaign manager for Mallory’s campaign.**
I want to be straight with you about where things stand with this Senate race. There are a lot of important Senate races on the map this year, but none are more important than Michigan — and I want you to know why.
Below is a memo on where things stand in our race. I hope you’ll take a moment to read it.
* * *
**CAMPAIGN MEMO**
**TO:** Team McMorrow
**FROM:** Wellesley Daniels
**RE:** What we’re up against
Mallory is up in the polls because she’s out talking about the issues that actually matter — like making sure we’re standing up to Trump and building a new American Dream where hard work pays off again. When people hear her vision _and_ her track record, they’re in, whether they’re a Democrat, Republican, or Independent.
Here’s the catch: The GOP knows it too. That’s why the Senate Leadership Fund, the biggest GOP super PAC out there, announced they’re spending **$45 million** on ads in Michigan. To put that in perspective, that’s more than they’re spending in Georgia, Iowa, and Alaska. And that’s not including the $1.5 million that AFP (a Koch-backed PAC) has already dropped on ads backing Mike Rogers.
The GOP is fixated on this seat because they know it’s their best shot to protect their Senate majority. One pundit put it pretty bluntly: _"If Michigan goes red, if Mike Rogers wins this race... the map is over."_
That’s why we’re not waiting around until Election Day to start fighting back. We have to define this race **right now.** Mallory is the best person for this job, but she can’t out-talk $45 million in dark money without some help.

subject: When Charlie said “35,000,” I laughed...
body:
Before you give up on America — read this| | | [](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=4d2c9217fd3c4d7ab85ac2dbd1bdd369&_e=sqeR6Ofe2xIGgpTBYPyIzaR8IHhgFy1AqTzbpW3fRpphbqCH2IehfXfZaKWzBbPcxFgeWbXVgfUBnO8xnjP5PV2kdfZs-tBQrqtxenp30NMs4LWnTMv5tkYKL0wiL6iaBM6LgHljz-Jl57vtMjAr4LWyCOe6gnqjPpMqs4zLBbS-UbU9O9fH7SNxRZ9y3b_KbzDLw3ICAvP4cB_xm8yxN5MkyOQJI7Wxq0-rF1Axj7h3w6vA2ho5DOD7qOy42bQCDEBDiBOS-K9X-9aHAzbnWHLz_nzEgXZNvLKvJW8DUnl39lnMT0ZED5Z21-Cu-Z0zPM0n7GeSqIznopvqtAhSVTtYRdC6zQjYPO_oMVRrst7Avi7pQil-u_ouMbKz1z0Oor2lI-4rF-hqZCFhnprcZidNwIEdDgV3kyi8kAsy661Dfj_umgf92bTbtnDe7ZnI8TGq0RMZUSNBAPu-t6kUh2I_rn9wrFy6bHtyHs3O9YCgjUY0kgkjGb4xxrAoiGa-2BjFqwE1yE_KcARFq6MmCMP1XtGcDL4eqAhaWtgiy16deY5fFvlBUyePAsKbp56xwsPawW6HOzXwDmuPjhMEjUtx2HHnWC-aaqYGvbA_4n1bnnvrbcd9ZyiOMOqLkWeB6tOCbrME71H9yqYdhkd540W4pLn3yLN9mabUn6HWfD8sidcLu3j8iV6ullHd8t0dKFinBOWeS8niKcsV-VBJpQ%3D%3D)
---
| | Patriot,
---
If you ever doubted we could win America's youth back from the Left...

If you ever wondered whether we'd lost the next generation for good...

If you ever sat up at night -- watching the news, seeing what's happening in our schools, our culture, our country -- and thought, _" Is it already too late?" _

You're not alone.

A lot of good people have been asking the same question.

**But I want to tell you something that might just change how you feel about the future of this country... **

Just one year ago, Turning Point USA's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.

That was no small feat.

Starting a single chapter today takes serious courage. Students get mocked. Threatened. Investigated. Sometimes even physically attacked.

So reaching 1,200 chapters already felt like a miracle.

_Then Charlie called me... _

He said: "Andrew, I love what we're doing with our high school program -- but we've got to move faster."

I told him, "We are."

Charlie replied, "No you're not thinking what I'm thinking... I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I laughed. I told him, "Charlie, there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said, "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

Without skipping a beat, Charlie said, "Okay, great. Let's do 27,000!"
I'll be honest -- I froze.

We didn't have the numbers. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the roadmap yet.

But he wasn't fazed.

He said, "Don't worry. We'll figure it out. We'll do it together."

That was Charlie.

He didn't think small. He didn't move slow. He didn't settle for "maybe someday."

He believed in going now.

And he believed that if the mission was right, the path would reveal itself.

He chased what others only dreamed about... and turned what others thought impossible into reality.

That's why he built Turning Point USA in the first place.

That's why tens of thousands of students were inspired by Charlie to start chapters of their own -- _many in schools where they were explicitly told not to. _

**And that 's why today -- less than a year later -- we're not in 1,200 schools anymore: **
---
[](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=4d2c9217fd3c4d7ab85ac2dbd1bdd369&_e=sqeR6Ofe2xIGgpTBYPyIzaR8IHhgFy1AqTzbpW3fRpphbqCH2IehfXfZaKWzBbPcxFgeWbXVgfUBnO8xnjP5PV2kdfZs-tBQrqtxenp30NMs4LWnTMv5tkYKL0wiL6iaBM6LgHljz-Jl57vtMjAr4LWyCOe6gnqjPpMqs4zLBbS-UbU9O9fH7SNxRZ9y3b_KbzDLw3ICAvP4cB_xm8yxN5MkyOQJI7Wxq0-rF1Axj7h3w6vA2ho5DOD7qOy42bQCsuj5hQVCepLrlHwF-9pvGGb1Ndu9duQ-Rxc_BGP3KotdaRojVra1jtQbCkVNn39DnddCFjAdE50_e8K5QJehJM-VXTCnS3KWlnc9JbDvMKZLEnsLqG-qcGfKvYCP975w05nNqslie36k4vbRe38AruM2HSvQYTYMhJ456uPbZpHudQUUVugV36JwB0rAYnEmNCOpUH7Vk2rqu1YRxFOmf--ZeDNzkA7eG76Xn1Q5qap2v1iZQC3LR8Jb8CPhAJfIm4XN0P5FioWYoulfd15pPYjjjXiie-jJ3_ezyKlcTSwe6GZCN70bNT6jSvQfc4S8pRjfl59jQt8XjYiGLOx4WdgMeCkkzsgjNLnzs2vCfwJMokQSzPgSfN5hJqD5X3b-hTGFaTcKmTAydmk55BjpyJ3M8tWaX0sJmLjUkEFBdj4NHkDyfXdwS_14FRBcdVWJJLigHO69UQlhTdAwIuhb-w%3D%3D)
---
We're in 3,300.

That's roughly 13% of all high schools in America.

Eight states have officially partnered with Club America to bring our chapters into every school statewide.

✅ Florida
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee
✅ Oklahoma
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Arkansas
✅ Indiana

And we're just getting started.

Think about that: 13% of America's youth now have a place at school where they can say it's okay to love this country...

That it's okay to be bold. That it's okay to believe in God, in family, and in freedom.

_That 's what Club America is about... _

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. clean_body: Safeguarding jobs, health, and humanity for Tennessee | Friend, As your next Governor, Jerri Green is committed to safeguarding our communities’ future, while ensuring that innovation works for us, not the other way around. From protecting our natural water supply to holding big tech accountable , Jerri is fighting for policies focused on the health, safety, economic well-being, and humanity of Tennesseans. Recently, xAI made the troubling decision to pause development of a greywater reuse facility, an essential part of their pledge to protect Memphis' most pressious natural resource, The Memphis Sand Aquifer. As a leader on the Memphis City Council,Jerri worked to make sure that companies like xAI will be held to standards of environmental responsibility. Now she’s demanding answers from xAI leadership and the Greater Memphis Chamber of Commerce. As Governor, Jerri will hold corporations accountable to the people of Tennessee , demanding transparency and measurable action on promises made. Jerri Green's reflects her long-standing commitment to protecting you and your family in this rapidly changing digital landscape. Here’s how she’ll do it: AI Literacy: Implement programs in schools to help students identify deepfakes and protect their mental health. Job Protection: Fine corporations that replace 25 or more workers with AI, using those funds for local job retraining. Energy Costs: Protect your electric bill by ensuring tech companies pay for their energy consumption, not local families. Water Conservation: Require tech companies to use recycled water to cool their servers, safeguarding our drinking water. AI Accountability: Ban AI from influencing rent hikes, job denials, and medical decisions, ensuring you always have the right to a human appeal. subject: The Autism Health Summit is Almost Here!
body:
** The 2026 Autism Health Summit is Almost Here!
------------------------------------------------------------

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JyPTtXfKYd8&mc_cid=bf2526a334&mc_eid=UNIQID

April 24–26, 2026 | Legacy Center Resort & Spa | San Diego, California

The countdown is on. With only 1 week to go, we are excited to welcome you to the Autism Health Summit, taking place April 24–26, 2026 in San Diego at the Legacy Center Resort and Spa. This powerful three-day event brings together leading experts, practitioners, researchers, and families for a weekend of education, collaboration, and meaningful conversation around autism and neurological health.

We want to share an important update with our community. While the San Diego Regional Center will not be sponsoring tickets for this event due to unforeseen circumstances, we remain deeply committed to accessibility. We are offering scholarships for low-income families who would like to attend. You must apply by April 15th to receive approval. HERE is the link (https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/autismhealth.com%2Fscholarships%2F/b43o/PqzEAQ/AQ/002bae49-e3a3-4d12-a039-d18eb34273d4/2/RCYM1tEp8p?mc_cid=bf2526a334&mc_eid=UNIQID) .

As we approach the final weeks, we invite you to take advantage of our current offer. Use promo code Autism50 to receive $50 off your in-person ticket.

We look forward to welcoming you to San Diego for an unforgettable weekend of education, empowerment, and community.
REGISTER HERE (https://ahsconference.com/pricing-table/?mc_cid=bf2526a334&mc_eid=UNIQID)

Earn CME Credits At the AHS Conference!
We are proud to offer Continuing Medical Education (CME) credits for medical professionals attending the Autism Health Summit. Participants who purchase a Professional Ticket will be eligible to receive 10.5 CME credits, providing valuable, evidence-informed education while fulfilling continuing education requirements. This is an excellent opportunity for physicians and healthcare providers to gain deeper insights into emerging research, clinical applications, and integrative approaches to autism and neurological health

Meet Our Headline Speakers!
https://ahsconference.com/?mc_cid=bf2526a334&mc_eid=UNIQID

This year’s Summit features an outstanding lineup of headline speakers, including Aaron Siri, Del Bigtree, Dr. Robert Malone, Dr. Toby Rogers, Dr. Sabine Hazan, and Dr. Dayan Goodenowe, along with many more respected voices in the field. Attendees will also hear from Ed Clay and his team at Cellular Performance Institute (CPI), who will share the latest updates and research surrounding their upcoming clinical trial for autism.
SPONSOR LINKS (https://ahsconference.com/sponsors/?mc_cid=bf2526a334&mc_eid=UNIQID)

Many Thanks to Our Sponsors!

We are deeply grateful to our top Diamond, Platinum, and Gold Sponsors for their continued support and leadership: Cellular Performance Institute (CPI), Dr. Goodenowe Enterprises, European Wellness, and Satellite Phone Store. Their commitment helps make this event possible and supports ongoing education and outreach within the autism community.

We also extend our sincere thanks to our Silver, Health, and Wellness Sponsors whose generosity and shared mission strengthen this work, including Functional Genomic Analysis, Neuro Needs, Microbiome Research Foundation, NutraMedix, Relax Saunas, MAHA Action, Best EMF Products, ARCC Center, Children's Health Defense, MyMycolab, Life Wave and Brain Tap, Daylight Computer Company, Weston A. Price Foundation, VibraTec Plates, Sun Power LED, Stalwart Law Group, DNA Academy, Function Medicine Georgia, Kadiant, Algonot, Informed Policy Advocates, Micronic Silver, SPELLERS, Spectrum Sciences LLC, The Wellness Blanket, Xlear, Vicar Venetia, Strategic Response Partners, Sabre Defense Team, Pur Health, LLC, Warrior Mom, Purium, C-Polar Technologies, OxyHealth, Solex AO Scan, Pulse PEMF, MAPS, PatchMD, CelWel, ReligenDX, Frequency+ Peptides, Mindset Kids, Mosaic Diagnostics, Leabs & Rebounds, Beautiful Minds Family Counceling, and Physicians for Informed Consent.
AHS AGENDA (https://ahsconference.com/agenda/?mc_cid=bf2526a334&mc_eid=UNIQID)

** Important Update for California Residents
------------------------------------------------------------

We want to bring your attention to an important piece of legislation impacting families across California.

SB 1377 will be heard by the Senate Health Committee on Wednesday, April 15th. This bill is focused on restoring critical rights within our healthcare system, including:

• Restoring physician autonomy in making medical decisions

• Reinstating fair and individualized medical exemption processes

• Protecting patients and families from discrimination

This legislation represents a meaningful step toward ensuring that medical decisions remain in the hands of qualified healthcare providers and are tailored to the unique needs of each individual.

The organization Informed Policy Advocates is actively working alongside the bill’s author, Brian Jones, to support a strong and well-informed presentation. Their efforts include providing critical data and connecting subject matter experts to help ensure this bill is thoroughly understood and thoughtfully considered.

We encourage our California community to stay informed and engaged as this important hearing approaches.
CLICK HERE FOR LINK (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260SB1377&nvep=&hmac=&emci=f750e2e6-a729-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=ea000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001&ceid=&mc_cid=bf2526a334&mc_eid=UNIQID)

About Autism Health Inc.
Autism Health is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to educating individuals, families, and communities about autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Autism Health provides educational programs, workshops, events, research, and resources tailored to meet the diverse needs of those impacted by autism and other neurological disorders.
DONATE HERE (https://autismhealth.com/donations/?mc_cid=bf2526a334&mc_eid=UNIQID)
Autism Health Inc. depends on generous donations from our community. Large or small, every donation gets us closer to achieving our goals. We are grateful for your assistance! For more information about Autism Health, visit www.AutismHealth.com

# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=41139%2E3422442%2EfdHZeQ)
Peter, it’s been just over two weeks since I kicked off the Whiteboard Warriors Tour, hosting town halls across the state—and I want to share exactly what I’ve been hearing.
**No matter where I go, the message is the same: working people are just stretched too thin. They’re doing everything right, and _still_ falling behind.**
I’ve talked to parents working full-time who still can’t afford child care. Small business owners who are barely hanging on while big corporations rake in record profits. Families watching their budgets tighten every month as rent keeps going up.
These are real problems happening in every corner of our state, and they won’t be solved by politicians who don’t live them.
I’m a single mom. I’ve had to budget every dollar, struggle to make cuts, and figure out how to make it all work. And I’ll tell you this: _the people in charge right now aren’t feeling that pressure—but they should be._
I’m running for governor to put working Californians first and tackle the affordability crisis head-on. That means single-payer health care, free child care, less expensive housing, and more.
**This tour is about more than just sharing my plan. It’s how I hear directly from Californians and fight to make these solutions real.**
And I’m doing it without taking a single penny from corporate PACs—because we deserve a governor who isn’t owned by billionaires or special interests.
**[But being on the road and hosting these town halls takes real resources. If you’re able, I’m asking you to chip in $5 or whatever makes sense to you today so I can keep reaching voters, hearing their stories, and fighting for a more affordable California.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260413_1_ak.uV4746&refcode=em20260413-41139&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41139%2E3422442%2EfdHZeQ)**

Thank you,
Katie

When President Trump **[ordered the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz](https://substack.com/redirect/948e9d9c-bfa6-40b6-9d02-17bd3392b3da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , the usual **[chorus of hand-wringing](https://substack.com/redirect/7cc84409-cb2b-433d-bbe1-dbe4bf53934e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** immediately began. Pundits and politicians warned of escalation, oil shocks, and global chaos. They missed the obvious. Trump wasn't inventing a new strategy. He was simply running the same playbook John F. Kennedy used in 1962 -- **only from a far stronger position.**
After weeks of threats and sporadic attacks on tankers, Tehran attempted to turn the Strait of Hormuz into a weapon, effectively closing the narrow chokepoint through which roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supply normally flows. They did it to squeeze the global economy and **try and force Trump 's hand.** In response, Trump did what any serious leader would do when an adversary tries to use the world's energy lifeline as leverage: **he shut the door on them.**
This is not recklessness. It is basic strategic logic. By blockading the strait, the United States has cut off Iran's single biggest source of income -- the sale of oil to countries willing to look the other way. Iran can no longer play favorites, letting friendly tankers through while holding the rest of the world to ransom. **That game is now over.**
The effects are already visible on two fronts. First, Iran is about to lose a major revenue stream. Second, and perhaps more importantly, the primary beneficiary of that Iranian oil -- China -- has just had its supply line turned off at the tap. Beijing has relied heavily on Iranian crude, especially after the collapse of once friendly Venezuelan production.
## [Was this Trump's Venezuela plan all along?](https://substack.com/redirect/19eea25a-9ce9-443e-a645-074818fd7ea3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Trump's blockade simultaneously starves Iran of cash and turns the screw on China. Iran's most important remaining patron and America's biggest national security concern.
This is not accidental, Iran has been using oil sales as quiet leverage to keep China tacitly "on its side," **[reportedly even exploring arms deals that would include Chinese air-defence systems.](https://substack.com/redirect/3149de58-5451-4455-ab58-2f039dfc350d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** As of this morning, that pipeline is closed. Trump has threatened 50% tariffs on any Chinese goods **if Beijing follows through with weapons shipments to Iran.** The message is unmistakable: the old arrangement where Iran sold oil quietly and bought weapons is finished.

Critics call the blockade dangerous, but they forget history. In 1962, President Kennedy imposed a naval quarantine on Cuba to prevent the Soviet Union from placing nuclear missiles on America's doorstep.
* **The world held its breath.**
* **The blockade worked.**
* **Khrushchev blinked.**
* **The missiles were removed.**

Kennedy understood that blockades can be precise, enforceable, and far less costly than full-scale war.
Trump is applying the same principle today, **only with better cards.** Unlike Kennedy, who was dealing with a superpower possibly willing to take the world to the brink of nuclear confrontation, Trump faces an Iranian regime that is already battered militarily and economically. Iran's navy has been largely sunk. Its command-and-control infrastructure has been shredded. Its proxies are reeling. Closing the Strait of Hormuz was supposed to be its ace in the hole. Instead, it has been served straight back at them. The net effect is substantial.

At the same time, he has reminded China that its dependence on Middle Eastern oil flows through waterways the United States can (and as of this morning, do) control. China is now about to go through the same oil recalculation that the rest of the world has been dealing with as they discover that solar and wind are not viable when not backed up by cheap Gulf oil.
The grip around the Iranian regime is tightening.
* **Its navy is crippled.**
* **Its oil revenue is drying up.**
* **Its major patron is being squeezed.**

Whether U.S. airstrikes resume after the failure of the Islamabad talks remains to be seen, but the strategic picture has already shifted. Iran played the strongest card it had by trying to weaponize the Strait of Hormuz. Trump has now played a stronger one by weaponizing the Persian Gulf.
## [Trump shook up the Middle East and that's a good thing](https://substack.com/redirect/3e38adc9-350f-4b24-a25b-8bbd4e11886e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

[The Persian Gulf has never been a peaceful trade route. For decades it has served as the Middle East's most dangerous poker table, where Iran has bluffed its way forward with proxies, gray-zone attacks, and nuclear hedging while the world's energy lifelines hung in the balance.](https://substack.com/redirect/3e38adc9-350f-4b24-a25b-8bbd4e11886e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

The political establishment may wail, but the results are already speaking for themselves: disrupted Iranian oil flows, rising pressure on China, and a regime that is slowly being denied access to it's its few remaining levers of power.
**[The US Navy not the British Royal Navy is now the guardian of the sea lanes](https://substack.com/redirect/d624fbe4-2cdd-4aaf-9b1a-46774fa0f6b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and the message is simple. When America decides a chokepoint will no longer be held hostage, it has the means and the will to enforce that decision.
Trump knows that blockades work. JFK already proved it.
Iran is learning Cuba's lesson**....the hard way.**

This fight will take all of us across the nation coming together to thwart Trump’s power grabs.
