Hungary just proved that even billionaire-backed authoritarian machines can be beaten--and every mini-Orban from Mar-a-Lago to Moscow should be sweating | | and | Apr 13 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | Cliff's Note: Thank you as always for reading, my friends. Hungary just showed the world that even one of the most polished authoritarian machines in the West can be beaten by those willing to stand up, put it all on the line, tell the truth, and fight every day. Paid subscribers make this work possible --the deeper dives, the historical context, the live conversations, and the moral clarity corporate media too often avoids. Help me keep connecting the authoritarian dots from Budapest to Mar-a-Lago.. | | ---|---|--- The Strongman Fell --As All Inevitably Do--And Autocrats Are Having Palpitations Worldwide by Cliff Schecter I'll never forget taking a trip to Romania as a consultant for the United States Information Agency's (State Department) democracy-promotion program in the mid-2000s. As part of my tour of Bucharest, we went to Revolution Square (Pia ța Revoluției) where bullet holes from the 1989 Romanian Revolution still scarred the visages of buildings around the square. It served as a reminder of how quickly the end can come for hubristic sociopaths hiding behind the title of "leader." Not that I was thinking of anyone specifically here. 😉 Nicolae Ceaușescu, the longtime Communist Dictator of Romania was executed Christmas day 1989. Just one week beforehand, he was (ironically, due to today's headlines) on a state trip to Iran like all was normal. He was ousted in no small part because he'd lost the people with draconian policies, like food and energy rationing. He had a massive debt to contend with, as a shrinking GDP and his taste for the finer things in life--which, to be honest, isn 't very communist-y--had gotten him in trouble: Ceaușescu became obsessed with building himself a palace of unprecedented proportions, along with an equally grandiose neighborhood, Centrul Civic to accompany it. Yes, as people were starving, the elite predator had himself constructed the second largest building--in surface area--in the world. The first? The Pentagon. There may be a message in that reality, too. But Ceaușescu wasn't satisfied with just one ridiculously lavish, enormous-arse palace, so he also built himself a whole neighborhood to surround it! Trump just put his name on the Kennedy Center so everyone could stop showing up and is constructing some little pissant ballroom. Donald, I didn't serve with Nicolae Ceaușescu. I didn't know Nicolae Ceaușescu. Nicolae Ceaușescu was no friend of mine. And you're no Nicolae Ceaușescu. | | ---|---|--- In any case, why do I bring this up? Because here we have a man who thinks he's a dictator, is just about the most openly corrupt leader ever seen, has pardoned and protected a pedophile in his ranks, and is wrecking the economy until jobs, food, and prices of essentials are all in the crapper. Oh, wait, you thought I meant Donald Trump?! Actually, I was talking about Orban! And now you see why Donald Trump should be terrified: ...a scandal rocked Fidesz in early 2024. Hungary's president at the time, Katalin Novak, pardoned a former official convicted of helping cover up abuse of underaged boys at a children's home. The revelation of the pardon punctured a perception of Orban's government...as the defender of Christian and family values. "The core of the self-definition of Fidesz is that they are conservative, family-friendly, and they protect children, " Peter Kreko, a political scientist who runs Political Capital, a think-tank in Budapest, told CNN. To many voters, the pardon scandal exposed the "hypocrisy" of the Orban project, Kreko said... In February 2024, Magyar gave an explosive video interview to Partizan, a Hungarian media outlet..to share information he gleaned from his proximity to government. " A few families own half the country," he said in the interview, viewed nearly 3 million times, in a country of fewer than 10 million people. While Orban's campaign this year revolved mostly around foreign policy and his relations with world leaders, Magyar 's was rigidly focused on domestic issues, such as the economy and corruption. Over the past two years, he worked to build a direct relationship with voters, visiting scores of towns and cities, and often staying for hours after his speeches to meet local people. | | ---|---|--- I dunno, Democrats, but it seems Magyar won by being authentic with voters, targeting predatory billionaires who own everything and extract the rest from the people, and calling out pedophilia protection and corruption. Then he added the final blow, how those who engaged in this despicable behavior wrecked the economy for all, and the welfare of regular Hungarians. I think we just may 've discovered a formula that beats fascist incumbents! (Psst: The one I've been screaming Democratic Leaders should adopt for a year now). ORBAN 'S TIMELY POLITICAL DEMISE For 16 years, Viktor Orban sold Hungarian elites--and much of the global right--a poisonous fantasy: that you could hollow out democracy, rig the media, enrich your cronies, flirt with Moscow, sneer at the European Union, even willingly spend time with the most unpleasant AI personality yet constructed, known as a "JD Vance." | | ---|---|--- And somehow call all this "the will of the people." Orban became Trumpism's favorite export model, the patron saint of "illiberal democracy," the guy every would-be autocrat in a suit and flag pin pointed to and said, see, this is how you do it. If that toad can pull it off, why not me? But now? He just got his clock cleaned. In a political earthquake, Peter Magyar's Tisza party didn't just beat Orban--they routed him, with the kind of parliamentary majority--nearly 70%!--that may finally give Hungary the tools to undo the constitutional vandalism Orban spent a decade and a half perfecting. What makes this defeat monumental--and by that I mean gorgeous!--isn't just the seat count. It's that Orban lost despite the authoritarian cheat codes he'd spent years installing like IEDs throughout this decaying democracy: media capture, gerrymandered districts, patronage networks, oligarch cash pipelines, and a political culture built on fear, grievance, and nationalist mumbo-jumbo. This wasn't some clean, level playing field where the voters merely changed their minds over an egg-white-omelet brunch. This was the Hungarian people kicking down in walls of a house Orban had spent years bolting shut from the inside. Record turnout--nearly 80% --tells the story better than any pundit ever could: people were done being ruled by a kleptocratic wannabe czar whose whole act had curdled into crony capitalism and Putin-smooching rot. But here's the best part: this is a flashing red warning light for the global predator class that has used Orb an as a test kitchen for democratic sabotage. Trumpworld adored him because he proved you could turn a democracy into a family office with better goulash and great grift. The far-right in Europe loved him because he weaponized culture war bile while quietly making his friends rich. Putin loved him because Orban functioned as Moscow's house ally inside the EU, blocking aid to Ukraine and muddying Europe's response to authoritarian assholes like...Putin. That entire axis of ego just took a major gut punch. Hungary choosing a pro-EU course under their new Prime Minister, Magyar doesn't just change Budapest--it reverberates through Brussels, Moscow, Washington, and every billionaire-funded nationalist project that thought the future belonged to strongmen. Somewhere Peter Thiel is very sweaty. Though, if you've seen him before, he's a constantly fiddling overactive sweat gland on a good day--like cocaine come to life. So I'm not sure you could tell the difference. The best part of all this? Orban's fall is a reminder that even systems built to protect power can crack when people stop accepting the lie that the strongman is inevitable. This is so important I'm tempted to repeat it. There is not guaranteed fate except for one we willingly accept. This is the lesson Democrats, pro-democracy coalitions, and frankly anyone fighting the billionaire predators running way-too-much of our world need tattooed on their frontal lobes: Like Ceaușescu, autocrats look invincible...until the day they don't. The edifice always appears permanent right up til the moment the people start puncturing it with bullet holes. Autocrats fall when people stop believing the myth of inevitability. Viktor Orban's defeat is bigger than Hungary. It's proof that billionaire-backed strongmen can be beaten, that oligarch cash and captured media don't make a regime immortal, and that democracy still has fight left in it. Knowing this, somewhere tonight, every mini-Orban from Moscow to Mumbai is suddenly sleeping a little less soundly. Hungary just showed the world that even one of the most polished authoritarian machines in the West can be beaten by those willing to stand up, put it all on the line, tell the truth, and fight every day. Retired Rear Adm. Mark Montgomery said the blockade "only works if the US Navy is persistent and stops and detains enough Iranian ships to deter the regime's ability to export fossil fuels."

name: Rashida Tlaib
subject: I don’t want to have to call my next senator and check them on their vote
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1001&akid=2008%2E251025%2Em9mNS1 ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1002&akid=2008%2E251025%2Em9mNS1 ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter, I'll be
honest with you. It’s exhausting demanding a Congress that truly
represents the people.

I've spent years having to beg my colleagues to do the right thing:

❌ Don't take money from corporations that are poisoning our neighborhoods.
❌ Don't fund wars that are killing innocent people.
❌ Don't vote to keep Big Pharma price-gouging your constituents.

And I'm tired of it.

That's why I'm going all in for Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate — and why
I'm asking you to join me by [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260413-2-ak.PjpHU5&amount=10&refcode=em20260413-2006&t=1004&akid=2008%2E251025%2Em9mNS1 ]splitting a donation to our campaigns.

I grew up in Southwest Detroit. I know what it means to have corporate
polluters dumping in your backyard while politicians look the other way. I
know what it's like to worry about ICE in your neighborhood, and go to
school where the ceiling tiles are falling.

Abdul also knows about everyday people’s struggles, and he did something
about it:

✅ He provided free glasses for thousands of kids in Wayne County.
✅ He cancelled $700 million in medical debt for 300,000 Michiganders.
✅ He didn't just talk about corporate greed. He fought it directly and
won.

In the U.S. Senate, Abdul will keep fighting for the people and winning.
And I won't have to babysit him. I won't have to check him on his vote. I
won't have to wonder whether he's going to act against our best interests
because some corporate PAC wrote him a check.

Abdul isn't taking a dime from corporate PACs. He’s the only candidate in
this race who never has and never will. That means when he gets to the
Senate, he answers to us — not corporations.

That also means he’s up against the full weight of the establishment and
outside groups who will spend whatever it takes to stop him.

They've already made it clear they'll spend millions to take out
candidates like Abdul, so now, we have to have his back.

This race is winnable. Abdul is polling near the top of this primary. But
whether we get him across the finish line comes down to grassroots support
— people like you, right now, showing up.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260413-2-ak.PjpHU5&amount=10&refcode=em20260413-2006&t=1005&akid=2008%2E251025%2Em9mNS1 ]Peter,
will you split a donation between Abdul and me today to help us get a U.S.
senator Michigan actually deserves?

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260413-2-ak.PjpHU5&amount=10&refcode=em20260413-2006&t=1024&akid=2008%2E251025%2Em9mNS1 ]Donate $10 ››

Thank you. Let’s go all in for Abdul and for the better world we can build
together!

In solidarity,

Rashida

[ Abdul ]Abdul and Rashida

| | Peter, can I take you back to where we started, and tell you about where we are now? | **2018:** I saw my community ravaged by gun violence, and saw the lives of 17 students and staff at Marjorie Stoneman Douglas High School taken, and began organizing with _March for Our Lives._

**2021:** I decided to take my organizing and activism to the next level, and run for office... If our politicians weren’t going to deliver change, our generation had to take things into our own hands.

**2022:** Despite not being taken seriously because of my age, I went on to win my primary by a large margin, against *nine* opponents. I became the first (and only!) Gen Zer elected to Congress.

**2023:** I worked with President Biden to establish the White House Office of Gun Violence Prevention, which was a huge step forward in our fight to end gun violence in our country.

**2024:** I went on a college campus tour, turning out Gen Z voters in Florida and all across America. Sadly, Trump was reelected, but we never gave up.

**2025:** I made it my mission to hold Trump and his Administration accountable in Congress. As long as they’re doing crazy sh*t, you can count on me to call them out.

**2026:** I’ve been fighting to expose this administration’s Epstein cover up, call out their fascism, all while organizing year-round and mobilizing young voters in Florida to flip the House blue this year.

If our politicians weren’t going to deliver change, our generation had to take things into our own hands. 2022: Despite not being taken seriously because of my age, I went on to win my primary by a large margin, against nine opponents. I became the first (and only!) Gen Zer elected to Congress. 2023: I worked with President Biden to establish the White House Office of Gun Violence Prevention, which was a huge step forward in our fight to end gun violence in our country. 2024: I went on a college campus tour, turning out Gen Z voters in Florida and all across America. Sadly, Trump was reelected, but we never gave up. 2025: I made it my mission to hold Trump and his Administration accountable in Congress. As long as they’re doing crazy sht, you can count on me to call them out. 2026: I’ve been fighting to expose this administration’s Epstein cover up, call out their fascism, all while organizing year-round and mobilizing young voters in Florida to flip the House blue this year. name: Chaz Molder
subject: What is a congressman supposed to do?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Molder for Congress
body:
It’s pretty simple when you stop overcomplicating it. Somebody should tell Andy Ogles.

| | | | |
---
Peter, I think somewhere along the way, people forgot what a congressman is actually supposed to do. The job is to represent the people in your district. That's it. It's not about building a brand, going viral, or getting booked on cable news. Being a congressional representative means picking up the phone when a veteran can't get their benefits sorted out. It means fighting for funding that keeps rural hospitals open. It means knowing what's happening in your district because you are actually there and talking to people. [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/TTI_0X9FFjBBu3GMYfX0PQ~~/AAUS1hA~/zyP_tzFmd1AWV9k5wxE61_-E3A8Kbf8goIrUa90btD4lIdrZyISJQ08dNGomTqTKaLstCkedq8VBqpa7oKvYoRBDv95PVc6-OK5xChdnVWM9MuiKXcIFeJeMjbilmRUjq2QCjvI8UgXAlE3HAL3Nt6MfKCunrvrNRkGHQA61LknZzoyL8FwFCVzV5aSxig40gLt1DCUqiMvn652IV3DOBPf_epaC02RIWwJYhsBRVxB2OW-gXHsEorb-lwZwiokn) Andy Ogles has had this job for a few years now, and I'm still not sure he knows what the job entails. He picks fights online, makes inflammatory comments that embarrass the district, and chases every national headline he can find. What he does not do is make life any better for the people he represents. I don't think that's a close call. I think most people in TN-5 can see it plain as day. As mayor, I've learned that the job is pretty simple when you stop over complicating it. You listen to people, you solve problems, and you answer to your community, not your followers. That's what a congressman should be doing. And that's what I'll do. We're approaching our mid-month fundraising goal, and hitting our goal means we can keep reaching more voters across TN-5. Last week, a new poll was released showing that **55% of Democrats** in this country think our party leadership has the “wrong priorities.”

That's staggering, but for most of us it’s not surprising.

What is surprising is the party’s refusal to do anything about it. At the DNC Spring Meeting's last Thursday, party leaders **rejected** a non-binding resolution to condemn AIPAC’s influence in our primaries.

name: Jim Jordan
subject: No one should ever accuse you of being a Democrat
body:
Insulting...
After all you’ve done for our Party, I salute you, Patriot!

| Patriot,
---
I’m sick of seeing text messages that accuse you of abandoning the GOP after all you’ve done for us.
---
All because you didn’t give $15 before some random deadline, that’s supposed to mean you **_“betrayed”_** the Republican Party and became a Democrat?
---
So all the times you stood in line to vote, you knocked on doors, you put up a yard sign, you made phone calls, you filled out surveys, you sacrificed your time and money – suddenly, all of that means nothing?
---
**_Give me a break! That’s just insulting._**
---
_Hand to God, I will never stoop to that low._
---
Truth be told, I try not to write too many emails and texts as it is. I’m busy working in Washington to do the job you asked me to do.
---
Honestly, fundraising just isn’t Priority #1.
---
At the end of 2024, I transferred $2.5 MILLION _**away**_ from my own campaign to help conservatives in tough races who _truly_ needed help.
---
**You know what I care about most?** The _ONLY_ thing that WINS elections – **_VOTES_**.
---
_That means registering voters, verifying every Trump voter’s profile, and constantly getting LIVE feedback from voters like you so that the President and I _always_ have the best, most accurate data in the country._
---

In a newly released video, Democratic candidate for Congress Rob Lucero is calling on his opponent, incumbent Rep. Jimmy Gomez, to suspend his reelection campaign. Gomez previously served as chairman of Eric Swalwell’s gubernatorial campaign and resigned only after allegations of sexual misconduct against Swalwell became publicly substantiated.

| | |
---
Hi Peter, In a newly released video, Democratic candidate for Congress Rob Lucero is calling on his opponent, incumbent Rep. Jimmy Gomez, to **suspend his reelection campaign**. Gomez served as **chairman of Eric Swalwell’s gubernatorial campaign** and resigned from that position only after allegations of sexual misconduct against Swalwell became publicly substantiated. Lucero points to reports that Swalwell openly bragged about his sexual behavior, raising questions about what those close to him—including Gomez—knew. While Gomez ultimately stepped down from the Swalwell campaign, Lucero argues that his years of silence while maintaining close ties to Swalwell warrant further scrutiny. “This is about accountability and trust,” Lucero said. “Voters deserve to know whether their elected officials ignored serious misconduct in their own circles.” Lucero’s video highlights these concerns and calls for greater transparency from those seeking public office. | | Friend, Last week, the President threatened to "destroy a whole civilization” overnight. It was a terrifying escalation and threat of a war crime in an irresponsible war with no end in sight. It also made one thing crystal clear: **the President is no longer in possession of himself.** For almost my entire life, our country has been embroiled in war in the Middle East. As a member of the House Armed Services Committee, I have a solemn obligation to protect the people in uniform from being used as pawns in an unauthorized, undefined war. I’ve seen the devastating toll these “forever wars” take on our families and national security. This isn’t about rhetoric; it’s about saving American lives. | | Each year as the months get warmer, Oregonians and westerners hold their breath to see what kind of wildfire season they'll be in for. It used to be that we could count on a few wildfires to ignite in late August or September, and be gone by the time fall rolled around. But over the last ten years, wildfires have grown significantly bigger, hotter, more frequent, and more dangerous to fight. And instead of fires starting in August or September, fires have started igniting earlier each year. This year, Oregon and the West are in for what's promising to be one of the most devastating fire seasons on record. Our state is experiencing record-low snowpack. Much of our state received just 11% of its normal pack. Crater Lake has the lowest snowpack in recorded history. These numbers are going to make Oregon's severe drought even worse. But that's not all. Last year, Trump and DOGE took a wrecking ball to wildfire preparation and firefighting operations. He defunded the federal programs that help states like ours prepare for and fight fires. 1400 qualified firefighting personnel left the Forest Service in 2025 and have yet to be replaced. And, just recently, it was announced that the Trump administration has decided to "reorganize the Forest Service." This sounds innocent enough, but just like everything else Trump has his hands on, the reality is far more sinister. Trump is replacing high-ranking fire officials with political appointees to do his bidding. He defunded 57 research stations, dedicated to researching the impacts of drought and forest management on wildfire risk. Let's be clear about what this is: Trump is gutting the Forest Service, safety of our communities be damned. He's gutting the agency and public servants that work tirelessly each year to protect our communities from and help us prepare for wildfires, just weeks away from what's promising to be one of the worst fire seasons in modern history. This is like needing open heart surgery and a few weeks before your operation, learning that the hospital has replaced your heart surgeon with Hannibal Lecter. Simply put: Oregon and Western states don't have the resources or firefighters we need for the upcoming season. **Donald Trump and JD Vance set us up to fail, and I fear the consequences will be catastrophic.** In the meantime, I'm going to continue fighting tirelessly to make sure our state gets what it needs to prepare for wildfires this summer. You might know me from Roots, Reading Rainbow, or Star Trek: The Next Generation. **Today, I’m more than proud to share that I'm endorsing my good friend Mandela Barnes to be the next governor of Wisconsin.** This is a critical moment in our country – no one can deny that. Mandela’s bold leadership is exactly what we need to tackle today’s problems with creative, innovative solutions. **[Will you chip in to Mandela’s campaign today?](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/1212?c0=mb-em-fr-apr26-mmfr.FkyFOx&amount=15&refcode=MB_EM_FR_041326_B2_MMFRLevarBurton&t=3&akid=6039%2E196590%2EIlfGRD)** I come from a family of educators, and it has been my life’s mission to make sure that future generations have the skills to learn, grow, and be civically engaged. And after hosting Reading Rainbow for more than 20 years on PBS, I was devastated to see federal funding for public broadcasting completely decimated. I believe that protecting services like these is vital. Hearing each other’s stories brings us together, fosters connection, and keeps us engaged with our communities. I know that as governor, Mandela is going to do just that. You don’t have to take my word for it — Mandela has an important story to tell. I look forward to seeing him on the campaign trail as he shares his vision for a Wisconsin where everyone can live up to their fullest potential. Friend,
If we want to lower costs, we need to tackle the real drivers— housing, utilities, and access to capital.
Rent and housing costs are too high. Utility bills keep going up. And small businesses are having a harder time getting loans from local banks.
That makes it harder to create jobs and grow our communities. This isn’t right.
I’m running for Congress because we need leadership that focuses on lowering costs and creating real opportunity:
* Building more housing so families can actually afford to live where they work
* Investing in infrastructure to bring down utility costs
* Supporting small businesses and restoring access to local capital
People should be able to afford a home, pay their bills, and build a good life here in Colorado.
We can make things better, but we have to fight for it.
If you're able to join our fight, will you chip in $15, $25, or whatever feels right today to help us keep going? [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/2604-q2-ak&amount=15]
